title: The Guest of the King's Hall
author: Calradia Remembers

binds.giver: the queen, wife of the ruler of a realm that is not the player's
binds.husband: her husband, the ruler of that realm

stages.journal: At the feast in {husband}'s hall, {giver}, queen of {giver_realm}, asked to speak with you away from the tables.
canvas: The feast is loud behind her. She has chosen a quiet place, and she speaks low, as one who is rarely alone.
She is the queen, and she carries it well; what she asks for is only a little of the guest's time, and she does not say why.
facts: She asks {player} to walk with her in the palace garden once the feast has thinned.
She is married to {husband}, who rules {giver_realm}.

stages.journal: Walk with {giver} in the palace garden, away from the feast.
canvas: The garden is dark and fragrant, the feast a murmur beyond the wall. She walks slowly, and for a while she speaks of nothing that matters.
Then, carefully, she speaks of her marriage: a crown chosen for her, a husband who rules well and does not see her. She does not complain; she describes.
facts: She is unhappy in her marriage to {husband}, though she never says a word against his rule.
She would meet {player} again, on the walls, when the hall is asleep, if {player} is willing.

{giver}: You asked {player} to walk with you in the garden, away from your husband's feast.
You have told no one else what you feel; you are not sure yet why you are telling this guest.
{husband}: {player} is a guest at your feast. You have noticed nothing out of the ordinary.

choices.label: Agree to meet her on the walls tonight

said.meaning: the player agrees to meet {giver} again, alone, on the walls tonight
the player declines to meet {giver} alone again and takes leave of her

choices.label: Let the feast end without an answer

stages.journal: {giver} waits for you on the walls of the palace, at night.
canvas: The walls at night, wind off the plain, the city asleep below. She came alone and she is cold, and she does not pretend otherwise.
She tells it plainly now: she would leave. Not for a crown, nor for gold. For a life of her own choosing, if the guest would take her away with them.
facts: She asks {player} to take her away from {husband}'s court.
She knows what it would mean: her husband would hold it as the gravest insult, and his realm would go to war over it.
A servant crossed the far end of the wall while they spoke; she cannot tell if he saw them.

{giver}: You met {player} alone on the walls at night and asked to be taken away from {husband}.
You know that if you leave, {husband} will go to war to have you back. You have weighed it, and you would still go.
{husband}: {player} is a guest at your feast. You know nothing of any meeting on the walls.

said.meaning: the player agrees to take {giver} away from {husband} and leave with her
the player refuses to take {giver} away, out of respect for {husband}'s hospitality

choices.label: Tell the king what his queen intends

said.meaning: the player tells {husband} that his queen {giver} means to leave him

choices.canvas: He hears it without a word at first. A king is told many things; this one he believes, and it costs him.

{husband}: {player}, a guest in your hall, has just told you that your queen {giver} means to leave you.

stages.journal: You left {husband}'s court with {giver}, and {giver_realm} takes up arms. Her return is the price of peace.

on_enter.summary: {giver}, queen of {giver_realm}, has left {husband} and rides with {player}. The king calls it an insult that only war can answer.

on_enter.text: My queen {giver} left my court with {player}, a guest I had fed at my own table. I will have her back, or I will have war.
I left {husband} and my crown and rode away with {player}. I chose it, and I knew the price.

canvas: She rides with you now, no longer a queen and not yet anything else. She knows what follows her: her husband's army, and the talk of every hall.

canvas.text: She does not regret it, and she does not pretend the war is nothing.

facts: {husband}'s realm is at war with {player}'s because {giver} left with {player}.
{husband} will make peace if {giver} is given back to him.

{giver}: You left {husband} and rode away with {player}. Your husband's realm is at war with {player}'s because of it.
You know that your return to {husband} is the price of peace.
{husband}: Your queen {giver} left your court with {player}. Your realm is at war with {player}'s over it.
You will make peace the day {giver} is given back to you, and not before.

choices.label: Give her back to {husband}
choices.journal: {husband} will make peace if {giver} is returned to him.

said.meaning: the player agrees to give {giver} back to {husband} in exchange for peace

choices.label: The war ends some other way

refused.memory: I asked {player} to take me away from {husband}'s court, and {player} would not betray the roof that sheltered them. I think the better of {player} for it, and I am still here.
refused.journal: You honoured your host. {giver} stays with her husband, and {husband} never knows what was asked.

no_answer.memory: I opened my heart to {player} at my husband's feast, and {player} rode away without an answer.
no_answer.journal: The feast ended, and you left {husband}'s court without giving {giver} an answer.

told.memory: {player} carried what I said in the night to my husband. I will not forget it.
told.journal: You told {husband} what his queen intended. He is grateful; she is not.

consequences.text: betrayed to my husband what I confided on the walls
{player}, a guest in my hall, warned me that my queen {giver} meant to leave me. I owe {player} for it.

returned.memory: {player} gave me back to {husband} so the war would end. I understood it. I have not forgiven it.
returned.journal: You gave {giver} back to {husband}. The war over her ends with her return.

consequences.summary: {giver} has been returned to {husband}, and the war fought over her ends.

consequences.text: {player} gave my queen {giver} back to me, and I made peace as I had sworn to.

she_died.journal: {giver} is dead. The war fought over her has lost its cause, if not its anger.

consequences.text: My queen {giver} died far from my court, beside {player}. I hold {player} to account for it.

he_died.memory: {husband} is dead. No one now can ask for my return; I am free of that crown at last.
he_died.journal: {husband} is dead. Nobody is left to claim {giver} back.

wed.memory: I married {player}. The way back to {husband}'s court is closed, and I closed it myself.
wed.journal: You married {giver}. There is no going back to {husband} now.

peace_otherwise.memory: The war over me ended without my return. I am still with {player}, and {husband} still remembers.
peace_otherwise.journal: The war with {husband}'s realm is over, and {giver} was never given back.
